diff --git a/cors.go b/cors.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..9e661ee
--- /dev/null
+++ b/cors.go
@@ -0,0 +1,243 @@
+package chi
+
+import (
+	"net/http"
+	"sort"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// CORSOptions configures the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing headers that
+// Mux#EnableCORSWithOptions and the CORS middleware write.
+//
+// A field left empty (or zero) writes no header for it, so an option is
+// switched off by clearing it.
+type CORSOptions struct {
+	// AllowOrigin is the value of Access-Control-Allow-Origin, either "*"
+	// or a single origin such as "https://example.com".
+	AllowOrigin string
+
+	// AllowMethods is the value of Access-Control-Allow-Methods on a
+	// preflight response. When it is empty the methods are detected from
+	// the routes registered for the requested path.
+	AllowMethods []string
+
+	// AllowHeaders is the value of Access-Control-Allow-Headers on a
+	// preflight response. When it is empty the headers the browser asked
+	// for in Access-Control-Request-Headers are allowed.
+	AllowHeaders []string
+
+	// ExposeHeaders is the value of Access-Control-Expose-Headers: the
+	// response headers a browser lets a page read beyond the safelisted ones.
+	ExposeHeaders []string
+
+	// MaxAge is how long, in seconds, a browser may cache a preflight
+	// response (Access-Control-Max-Age). Zero or less writes no header.
+	MaxAge int
+
+	// AllowCredentials writes Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.
+	// Browsers refuse a wildcard origin together with credentials, so the
+	// request's own Origin is answered in place of "*" when this is set.
+	AllowCredentials bool
+}
+
+// DefaultCORSOptions returns the options that Mux#EnableCORS uses: any
+// origin, the headers that browsers and JSON APIs commonly send, the
+// methods detected from the routes, and a preflight cache of one hour.
+func DefaultCORSOptions() CORSOptions {
+	return CORSOptions{
+		AllowOrigin: "*",
+		AllowHeaders: []string{
+			"Accept", "Authorization", "Content-Type", "Origin", "X-CSRF-Token", "X-Requested-With",
+		},
+		MaxAge: 3600,
+	}
+}
+
+// CORS returns a middleware that writes the CORS response headers described
+// by options and answers preflight requests itself.
+//
+// A preflight is an OPTIONS request for a path that has routes. It is
+// answered with 204 and the methods those routes have, in
+// Access-Control-Allow-Methods, without reaching the handler. An OPTIONS
+// request that has no Access-Control-Request-Method and whose path has its
+// own OPTIONS route is not a preflight, so it goes on to that route.
+//
+// The methods are found through the routing context of the request, so the
+// middleware knows them only behind a chi router; elsewhere it answers a
+// preflight only if options.AllowMethods names the methods.
+func CORS(options CORSOptions) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
+	return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
+		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+			setCORSHeaders(w, r, options)
+
+			if r.Method == http.MethodOptions {
+				if methods, ok := preflightMethods(r, options); ok {
+					writePreflight(w, r, options, methods)
+					return
+				}
+			}
+			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// corsMethodNotAllowedHandler is the method-not-allowed handler that
+// Mux#EnableCORSWithOptions installs. It is where a preflight ends up when
+// the CORS middleware did not see it first, as with a group made by
+// WithCORS, whose middleware runs only for routes that matched. Any other
+// method gets the 405 of next, or a plain 405 where there is none, with the
+// Allow header that RFC 9110 requires of a 405 response.
+func corsMethodNotAllowedHandler(options CORSOptions, next http.HandlerFunc) http.HandlerFunc {
+	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		methods := availableMethods(r)
+		if r.Method == http.MethodOptions && len(methods) > 0 {
+			setCORSHeaders(w, r, options)
+			writePreflight(w, r, options, methods)
+			return
+		}
+
+		if w.Header().Get("Allow") == "" {
+			if allow := methodList(methods); allow != "" {
+				w.Header().Set("Allow", allow)
+			}
+		}
+		if next != nil {
+			next(w, r)
+			return
+		}
+		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
+		w.Write(nil)
+	}
+}
+
+// set
